title: On-call roster governance
summary: Operator-owned governance of the on-call roster: who holds primary / secondary / manager tiers per shift window, how rotation handoffs are scheduled, and the binding the paging system reads at page time. The control is satisfied when every shift window has a non-empty roster resolution and a bound escalation chain prior to the window opening. Evidence is the bound chain emitted by the on-call-rotation playbook's bind-escalation-tiers step.

component.title: On-call rotation programme
component.description: Operator-managed rotation programme that schedules responder coverage, resolves the active escalation chain per shift window, and publishes the binding to the paging system before the window opens.

control-implementations.description: Implements the responder-readiness slice of the incident-response control family and the account-management slice of access control.

implemented-requirements.description: Incident handling capability: maintain a documented responder roster with defined escalation tiers so an incident is assigned to a responsible owner without delay.
Incident response assistance: secondary and manager escalation tiers provide guaranteed reach-back when the primary responder cannot acknowledge within policy.
Account management: rotation handoffs are tracked as account-state changes against the responder identities so role transitions remain auditable.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — IR-4 Incident Handling, IR-7 Incident Response Assistance, AC-2 Account Management
ENISA — Good practices for incident response and on-call readiness
MITRE D3FEND v1.0.0 — D3-AM Account Monitoring
